rows.h: 'auto' uses every visible NVIDIA GPU (CPU only if there is none), 'cpu' forces CPU, or give explicit GPU ordinals such as [0, 1].
Live-probe VRAM at startup even when a tuned hardware profile already exists.
Threads used for image ingest and the CPU-only modules; 'auto' leaves two cores free.
Replace every model with a deterministic synthetic stand-in so a run can be exercised with no weights and no GPU.
Let onnxruntime silently drop to the CPU provider instead of failing when CUDA will not load.
Extra LD_LIBRARY_PATH entries so onnxruntime can find the CUDA libraries; 'auto' resolves them from the installed torch wheels.
Execution providers to offer onnxruntime in order; 'auto' picks CUDA then CPU.
Numeric precision for GPU inference; fp16 is roughly twice as fast, fp32 is the safe fallback.
Try the TensorRT execution provider for ONNX models; falls back to CUDA when unavailable.
Hard ceiling on concurrent model workers placed on a single GPU.
Fixed per-worker VRAM budget; 'auto' uses the measured peak from the hardware profile.
Megabytes held back on every GPU for the driver and other processes.
Fraction of each GPU's free memory LM3 is allowed to plan against.
Worker count for any module without its own override; 'auto' derives it from the hardware profile.
Worker count for the pure-CPU ruler lattice conversion-factor module.
JPEG quality of the converted working copies, 100 being visually lossless.
Long-side pixel cap for the working copy every module sees; larger originals are downscaled once at ingest.
Class list in the exported model's own order; edit only when you swap in a model trained on a different set.
Minimum score a detection needs to be kept.
Reject the lower-confidence box of any same-class overlapping pair, since the detector is NMS-free and can emit duplicates.
'min' measures intersection over the smaller box, which catches nested duplicates; 'iou' is the standard intersection over union.
Overlap at or above which two same-class boxes count as duplicates.
Detect the non-plant items on the sheet: rulers, labels, barcodes, color cards, and more.
Square input size the detector letterboxes each sheet into; larger sees smaller items but costs more time and VRAM.
Overlap threshold used when merging competing boxes.
Ceiling on boxes kept per sheet.
Boxes smaller than this many pixels of area are discarded as noise.

Save the rectangular matrix view of each leaf's transform.
Compute the Euler Characteristic Transform shape signature for each oriented whole leaf.
Also keep the raw un-normalized pixel outline in the data file.
Punch insect holes out of the lamina instead of filling them in.
Add the petiole to the shape; leaving it off measures the lamina alone.
How many angular directions (and thresholds) the transform sweeps; more gives a finer signature and a bigger file.

Save the polar view with the leaf outline drawn on top, tip up in both.

Place the 31-keypoint leaf skeleton (midvein, apex, base, width, petiole) on each leaf crop.
Square input size for each leaf crop fed to the pose model.

Overlap threshold used when merging competing pose detections.
Artifact kind at that path; it must match the file you pointed at.

Derive lamina length, width, apex and base angles, and curvature from the keypoints.
Keypoints below this score are treated as absent and the metrics that need them stay empty.
Find the rotation that stands each leaf upright with its tip up, which the oriented exports and the ECT depend on.
Keypoint score floor for the tip and base points that define the upright axis.
How many midvein keypoints the principal-axis fallback needs when the tip or base is missing.
Minimum score a mask instance needs to be kept.
Trace the lamina, petiole, and holes inside every leaf crop.
Square input size for each leaf crop; larger gives finer mask edges at more cost.

Produce masks at the crop's own resolution instead of the model's coarser grid.
Convert the stored pixel measurements to centimeters using each sheet's conversion factor.

Measure area, perimeter, and the rotated bounding box of each segmented mask.
Only used by the lm2 method: run its rotate-to-minimum-circle search.
Algorithm that finds each leaf's long axis; pca is the area-weighted principal axis and is the most robust across leaf shapes.
Predict a rough conversion factor from image resolution alone; it runs first and anchors the ruler measurements.
